title: PAF-Enc: Position Affine Encoding to Reduce Bit-Flips in Non-Volatile Main Memories
problem: Emerging non-volatile memories (NVMs) used as main memory suffer from reduced lifetime and performance due to high write operations. Bit disparity between stored and incoming data creates unnecessary write operations, accelerating wear and limiting system lifespan.
motivation: DRAM scalability faces challenges with modern data-intensive workloads. NVMs offer superior density and energy efficiency but are limited by write endurance. Reducing bit-flip operations during writes directly improves NVM lifetime, performance, and enables their practical deployment as main memory.
method: Two-stage position-affine encoding (PAF-Enc) technique: (1) analyze memory data patterns to generate affine masks; (2) encode incoming cache blocks using XOR operations with masks to maximize resemblance to stored data before write, reducing bit disparity and write operations.
key_novelty: Position-affine encoding scheme that pre-processes incoming data to match existing memory patterns, significantly reducing bit-write operations; lightweight implementation using XOR operations.
contributions: PAF-Enc encoding technique for reducing unnecessary bit-write operations
Significant bit-write reduction through memory-pattern-aware encoding
Lightweight implementation with minimal overhead (XOR-based operations)
Improved NVM lifetime through reduced endurance degradation
Improved NVM performance through reduced write latency and power

metrics.primary: bit-write reduction (quantitative value not specified in abstract)

limitations: Abstract only; quantitative metrics for bit-write reduction not provided; memory overhead for pattern storage and masks not characterized; performance/latency impact of encoding step not analyzed; NVM technology variants not specified; comparison with other wear-reduction techniques missing; experimental validation not detailed.
